qti-assessment-test.title: CDEWorld - DEA MATE Act Acute Dental Analgesia & Dental Unit Waterline Infection Control (AGD PACE Self-Study Demo)

qti-assessment-item.title: Select evidence-based first-line analgesia for acute post-extraction dental pain under ADA and DEA MATE Act guidance.

qti-item-body.p: Objective: Select evidence-based first-line analgesia for acute post-extraction dental pain under ADA and DEA MATE Act guidance.

qti-choice-interaction.qti-prompt: A healthy 26-year-old patient with no hepatic, renal, or GI contraindications undergoes surgical extraction of an impacted mandibular third molar. Which post-operative analgesic regimen aligns with ADA clinical practice guidelines?
qti-choice-interaction.qti-simple-choice: Prescribe or direct a scheduled combination of ibuprofen 400 mg plus acetaminophen 500 mg every 6 hours as needed for acute inflammatory pain, reserving opioids only for breakthrough refractory cases after PDMP check.
Initiate extended-release oxycodone for 7 days so serum opioid levels remain steady during bone healing.
Provide a 30-tablet hydrocodone/acetaminophen supply without checking the state PDMP because dental extractions are acute procedures.
Combine ketorolac with high-dose ibuprofen concurrently to double COX-1/COX-2 inhibition.

qti-content-body.p: Correct. Randomized dental pain trials show combined NSAID + acetaminophen provides superior analgesia with fewer adverse events than opioid combinations, matching ADA first-line guidance.
Incorrect. Extended-release/long-acting opioids are contraindicated for acute post-procedural dental pain due to overdose and respiratory depression risk.
Incorrect. Excessive tablet counts create leftover diversion reservoirs and bypass mandatory PDMP controlled-substance checks.
Incorrect. Stacking two systemic NSAIDs markedly elevates GI bleeding and acute kidney injury risk without additive analgesic ceiling benefit.

qti-assessment-item.title: Enforce CDC sterile irrigant vs. dental unit waterline standards during oral surgical procedures.

qti-item-body.p: Objective: Enforce CDC sterile irrigant vs. dental unit waterline standards during oral surgical procedures.

qti-choice-interaction.qti-prompt: An oral surgery team prepares to section an impacted tooth and remove alveolar bone using a surgical bur. Which irrigant delivery setup complies with CDC dental infection-control guidelines?
qti-choice-interaction.qti-simple-choice: Deliver sterile saline or sterile water via a dedicated surgical irrigation pump with sterile single-use or heat-sterilized tubing, bypassing conventional dental unit waterlines.
Flush the conventional dental unit waterline for 20 seconds before surgery and use municipal tap water through the standard high-speed handpiece.
Pour sterile saline into the dental unit's self-contained water bottle and deliver it through existing unsterilized unit tubing.
Accept any dental unit waterline test result under 5,000 CFU/mL as compliant for both restorative and surgical procedures.

qti-content-body.p: Correct. Procedures that incise soft tissue or expose bone require sterile irrigating solutions delivered through sterile pathways because conventional dental unit waterlines cannot reliably guarantee sterility.
Incorrect. Flushing transiently lowers planktonic counts but does not render conventional waterline output sterile for bone surgery.
Incorrect. Passing sterile fluid through biofilm-colonized conventional unit tubing immediately recontaminates the irrigant.
Incorrect. Routine nonsurgical DUWL output must be <= 500 CFU/mL, and surgical bone procedures require sterile irrigant (0 CFU).

qti-assessment-item.title: Execute corrective shock-treatment and retesting workflows when DUWL monitoring exceeds 500 CFU/mL.

qti-item-body.p: Objective: Execute corrective shock-treatment and retesting workflows when DUWL monitoring exceeds 500 CFU/mL.

qti-choice-interaction.qti-prompt: Quarterly heterotrophic plate-count testing on Operatory 3's dental unit waterline returns 1,800 CFU/mL despite daily low-level maintenance tablets. What is the required infection-control remediation sequence?
qti-choice-interaction.qti-simple-choice: Take the affected waterline out of clinical use or switch to an alternate compliant source, perform manufacturer-validated shock disinfection to disrupt mature biofilm, and verify <= 500 CFU/mL by retesting before resuming routine use.
Double the concentration of daily maintenance tablets while continuing patient care and wait until next quarter's scheduled test.
Average Operatory 3's count with three other operatories that tested at 50 CFU/mL so the clinic mean stays below 500 CFU/mL.
Run hot tap water through the handpiece for 60 seconds each morning in place of chemical shock treatment.

qti-content-body.p: Correct. Continuous low-level maintenance agents cannot eradicate established biofilm once counts breach 500 CFU/mL; shock treatment plus documented pass retesting is required.
Incorrect. Off-label tablet doubling neither clears mature biofilm reliably nor protects patients during the intervening 90 days.
Incorrect. Waterline compliance applies per individual dental unit/line, never as a clinic-wide average.
Incorrect. Warm tap water promotes biofilm proliferation in narrow-bore tubing rather than disinfecting it.
